headline: TOUR WEEK OPENS: SCOUTS IN FIELDS, PRICES QUIET
subheadline: Pro Farmer crop tour begins today with corn and beans barely moving; Crop Progress at 3 PM CT resets the week.
lead: The Pro Farmer Crop Tour put boots in the Belt this morning and the market is doing what markets do before a verdict: nothing. Corn at $4.59 off a fraction, beans at $11.81 up a nickel, wheat the only real mover at $6.67, down 7 cents. Crop Progress at 3 PM CT is the first live number of the week.
the_takeaway: Wait on new positions; the tour and Crop Progress together write this week's price story.
teaser: Scouts are sampling fields right now. The board isn't moving until they talk.

one_number.unit: EIA forecast 2026 US natural gas production
one_number.context: That would be a record, above 2025's 118.5 Bcf/d. More supply into a market where natural gas already sits at $2.66 near the bottom of its 52-week range keeps input-cost pressure off grain drying and ammonia this fall.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called December corn down toward $4.72. December corn settled at $4.84 today -- never threatened that level.
yesterdays_call.note: Corn did not cooperate; $4.84 held comfortably above the $4.72 target. Miss owned. Tour week opens with December corn still needing a catalyst to break lower.

sections.title: GRAINS MARK TIME BEFORE TOUR DATA
sections.body:
- Corn at **$4.59** nearby and $4.84 December barely moved, down a fraction; the board is waiting on scout samples from Indiana and Ohio today before committing to a direction.
- Wheat gave back 7 cents to $6.67, reversing part of Friday's run without a fresh catalyst, which puts Friday's strength in the "position-squaring" column rather than a demand story.
- Crop Progress at 3 PM CT is the first live number; corn condition holding above last week's rating would remove a little weather premium still baked into December.
sections.catalyst: Pro Farmer Crop Tour underway Aug 17-20; Crop Progress due 3 PM CT today.
sections.bottom_line: No scout data yet, no move worth chasing. Wait for the 3 PM print.
sections.farmer_action: Old-crop corn: hold. Wednesday's scout summary is still your exit trigger if ears come in above 182 bu/acre.

sections.title: BEANS FIRM; TOUR IS THE REAL TEST
sections.body:
- Soybeans at **$11.81** nearby and $11.96 November are the quiet winners this morning, up 5 cents, with the China trade deal backstop (the $17 billion annual US ag purchase commitment, May 18, through 2028) keeping a floor under the board.
- Pod counts and pod fill from this week's scouts will tell you whether $11.96 November has room to push toward $12 or gets sold back to $11.74; that range defines the week.
- No fresh export news this morning, so the beans' nickel gain is positioning ahead of tour data, not demand.
sections.catalyst: Pro Farmer scouts in pod-fill fields today; China purchase backstop keeps bids supported.
sections.bottom_line: Beans above $11.94 November on strong pod counts is the trade; below $11.74 on disappointing scouts, carry breaks.

sections.title: CATTLE SLIP; STRUCTURAL STORY INTACT
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$223.62** dropped 1.1%, the weakest performer in the complex today, as fund liquidation continued after last week's exit with no new box-beef cutout news to reverse the flow.
- Feeders at $340.82 held better, off only 0.6%, which tells you the underlying feeder supply story, still processing-constrained by the Cargill multi-plant lockout ongoing since May 19 (roughly 6,000 head of daily capacity removed), is not broken.
- The screwworm-driven Mexican border closure, with the first phased reopening set for Aug 24 at Douglas, AZ, is seven days out; the feeder/live spread will tell you how fast the market prices returning supply.
sections.catalyst: USDA-DHS MOU on screwworm border protections announced; Aug 24 Douglas reopening on the calendar.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle selling is funds, not fundamentals; the Aug 24 border date is the structural reset to watch.

sections.title: CRUDE FIRMS; HORMUZ STILL IN PLAY
sections.body:
- WTI at **$82.52**, up 0.3%, with Hormuz tanker traffic slowing further over the weekend, the Iran-Hormuz cycle that re-escalated in early July and has since partially deflated is grinding higher again as Asian refiners now ask Saudi Aramco to reroute crude pickup to Egypt's Mediterranean port of Sidi Kerir.
- Natural gas at $2.66 drifted off 0.3%; EIA's record 2026 production forecast of 122.5 Bcf/d keeps any rally capped and fall fieldwork energy costs relatively tame.
sections.catalyst: Hormuz tanker traffic report (oilprice.com, 5h ago); Asian refiner rerouting request to Aramco.
sections.bottom_line: Crude input costs creeping higher on Hormuz, but gas stays cheap; net effect on fall fieldwork is neutral for now.

outside_the_pit.title: Rail Merger Rejection Sought by Major Grain Shipping Groups
outside_the_pit.body: Grain shippers including the Soy Transportation Coalition say Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern have not met minimum service standards in their revised merger application. A combined railroad could reduce competitive routing options and lift freight rates on export corridors at exactly the wrong time for a big 2026 crop looking for homes.

outside_the_pit.title: Fertilizer Prices Projected to Stay Elevated Through 2028
outside_the_pit.body: Feedstuffs reports geopolitical conflict and supply-chain disruption will keep fertilizer prices high well into the next crop cycle. Producers planning 2027 acres should treat current input quotes as the floor, not the ceiling, and lock what they can on fall anhydrous runs.

weekly_thread.question: What will Pro Farmer scouts find, and does the tour push December corn above $4.90 or back below $4.75 by Friday?
weekly_thread.status_text: Scouts hit the field today; Crop Progress at 3 PM CT is the first data point. The answer arrives in scout summaries Wednesday and the national number Friday Aug 21.

the_more_you_know.title: The rail bottleneck that shows up after harvest, not before
the_more_you_know.body: Grain shippers lose negotiating leverage the moment harvest starts: elevators fill, trucks back up, and railroads know it. The Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger fight matters most in October and November, when a single dominant carrier on key export corridors can widen the basis spread between the country elevator and the Gulf. Watch basis, not just the board.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn condition holding steady or better removes weather premium; a decline of 3+ points in good-excellent adds it back.
Pro Farmer eastern corn belt scout summary: above 182 bu/acre softens the board; below 178 adds December premium toward $4.90.
Weekly export sales: beans under 300K MT keeps tour data in charge of the story; above 500K MT validates the $11.96 November level.
Douglas, AZ port reopening for Mexican feeder cattle: feeder/live spread narrowing ahead of that date signals the market is already pricing returning supply.

daily_quote.text: What the fool does in the end, the wise man does in the beginning.

source_summary: USDA WASDE Aug 12, 2026; Pro Farmer Crop Tour (in progress Aug 17-20); CME settlement prices Aug 15, 2026; oilprice.com (Hormuz traffic, Aug 17); EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook Aug 2026; feedstuffs.com (fertilizer outlook); brownfieldagnews.com (rail merger, cattle futures); USDA-DHS MOU announcement.
